sentences.text:
The present application under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, has been filed to quash the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 22845/9 of 2024, (State Vs. Akash and another)
arising out of Case Crime No. 155 of 2024, under Sections 406, 420, 506 of I.P.C., Police Station- Chappar, District- Muzaffarnagar, as well as cognizance/ summoning order 26.11.2024 pending in the Court of Additional Chief Magistrate, Ist, Muzaffarnagar

Learned counsel for the applicants fairly admits that impugned F.I.R. has been lodged with regard to breach of trust of amount which Akash And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102203720/
1 was recovered form the members of the society.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicants are employee of the company Bharat Finance Company Ltd.
The F.I.R. has been lodged by the aforesaid finance company.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that applicants were not arrested during the course of investigation and the charge-sheet have been submitted against them.
It is further submitted that the offence is punishable up to 7 years imprisonment.
Upon considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the prayer made by learned counsel for the applicants is, hereby, refused.
After some arguments, learned counsel for the applicants wants to withdraw the application with liberty to file a regular bail application before the court of competent jurisdiction.

In case bail application is filed by the learned counsel for the applicants, the same shall be decided in the light of the observations made in the judgment rendered by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Another, (2022) 10 SCC 51, wherein the Supreme Court considering the category(A) as mentioned in the paragraph no. 2, bail applications of such accused against which charge-sheet has been submitted on appearance may be decided without the accused being taken in physical custody or by granting interim bail till the bail application is decided.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Another, (2022) 10 SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been observed that at the cost of repetition, we wish to state that, in category A, one would expect a better exercise of discretion on the part of the court in favour of the accused.
The application stands disposed of with the aforesaid liberty.
